field_name: Temporal Information Retrieval for Versioned Texts in Question Answering

categories.name: Query Expansion Techniques
categories.description: Methods that expand queries using generated text, embeddings, or pseudo-relevance feedback to improve retrieval effectiveness.

categories.name: Temporal Information Retrieval
categories.description: Approaches that model temporal aspects (e.g., recency, time constraints) in retrieval, often balancing relevance and time signals.

categories.name: Efficient Retrieval
categories.description: Techniques that reduce online latency via offline precomputation, approximate methods, or lightweight models.

categories.name: Temporal Graph / Expert Finding
categories.description: Methods that construct temporal graphs based on citation, author, or occurrence to model document relevance over time.

categories.name: Question Answering over Regulatory Documents
categories.description: QA systems tailored for regulatory, legal, or policy documents, often considering document structure and versioning.

idea_position: Temporal Information Retrieval (specifically applied to versioned regulatory documents for open-domain QA)
dominant_approaches: Learned gating mechanisms to dynamically balance semantic and temporal signals (e.g., Re3)
Temporal graph modeling based on document relationships over time
Offline precomputation of relevance weights for efficient retrieval
Query expansion using embeddings or generated text
common_assumptions: Each document version has a valid timestamp indicating enactment or amendment time.
Queries are associated with a target date (the time the question is asked).
Semantic similarity (e.g., from dense retrievers) provides a useful baseline for relevance.
Temporal relevance can be modeled as a function of time difference (e.g., decaying function).
Combining temporal and semantic signals can improve retrieval for time-sensitive queries.

repeated_limitations.description: Assumes explicit or reliably extractable timestamps, which may not hold in all settings.
Evaluation limited to specific domains (e.g., web, news), lacking generalization to other areas like scientific literature or regulatory texts.
Reliance on external components (e.g., neural re-rankers) adds complexity and latency.
Latency may increase with large candidate pools when using re-ranking or complex temporal modeling.

underexplored_combinations: Applying learned temporal relevance gating (like Re3) to versioned regulatory documents for QA
Combining temporal graph methods with semantic retrieval for expert finding over regulatory versions
Integrating query expansion with temporal relevance for handling hallucinations in versioned text QA
Using offline precomputation (like CORW) to enable efficient temporal-semantic retrieval over large versioned corpora
